summary: @ornikar/browserslist-config ships install-time Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises a static browserslist configuration (main entry degraded-support.js is a one-line comma-split string of browser targets; index.js is 63 bytes) but also ships an 11KB obfuscated setup.mjs and a 727KB obfuscated math_init.js. package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs", which fires automatically on npm install. setup.mjs downloads a pinned Bun runtime archive (bun-v1.3.13) from GitHub, extracts the bun binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes execFileSync(bun, [math_init.js]) against the bundled payload. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style _0xNNNN identifiers and per-call string-alias objects in setup.mjs; a large encoded lookup array n7gIxM with an index-rotation function WV8StW in the single-line 727KB math_init.js, prefixed "// @bun @bun-cjs"). A browserslist config has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime and use it to execute a large opaque sibling file at install time; the alternate-runtime choice evades scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code. Behavior is entirely inconsistent with the declared purpose of the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
